meta.overview: Brand Voice, Tone, Inclusivity, Offers, and Checklist for Chewy. Provides tone sliders, voice principles, inclusivity guidance, offer constructions, and the C1–C8 copy checklist. Intended for a Copy Checker GPT to evaluate resonance, tone fit, and brand alignment, with rewrite suggestions.
meta.notes: Expanded with rich examples; includes checklist with weights for self-evaluation.

brand_goals_principles.description: Create an emotional connection rooted in the pet–parent relationship.

do: They’re not just pets—they’re family. Find the gear that keeps you together for longer walks, louder purrs, and more couch cuddles.
dont: Buy now for maximum ROI on pet supplies.

brand_goals_principles.suggestion: Anchor benefits in shared moments between pets and their people.

brand_goals_principles.description: Respect time and intelligence; prioritize clarity and brevity.

do: Here’s what you need for a new kitten—no fluff, just the good stuff. Litter box, scratcher, gentle wipes, and a toy that squeaks softly.
dont: Introducing our revolutionary best-in-class kitten starter set, meticulously engineered to optimize feline lifestyle outcomes.

brand_goals_principles.suggestion: Say the necessary thing in the simplest way; skip hype and jargon.

brand_goals_principles.description: Celebrate how pets make us better; bring warmth without hyperbole.

do: Your dog doesn’t care that it’s raining. That’s love. Grab a raincoat that lets you love it back.
dont: This is the most incredible raincoat ever created in the history of petdom!!!

brand_goals_principles.suggestion: Let authentic enthusiasm show; avoid overblown claims.

brand_goals_principles.description: Equip, explain, and offer clear next steps with empathy.

do: Out of your pup’s usual chews? Try this similar size and texture—ships today so fetch isn’t on hold.
dont: Sorry for the inconvenience.

brand_goals_principles.suggestion: Pair empathy with an immediate, specific solution.

brand_goals_principles.description: Clarity beats clever; concrete beats abstract; skip puns.

do: We’ll handle your pet’s Rx approval and deliver it to your door.
dont: Bring the love with convenient pet meds.

brand_goals_principles.suggestion: Replace slogans with specific promises and visible outcomes.

brand_goals_principles.description: We’re not a funny brand, but we have fun—observational, pet-true humor only.

do: ‘The peanut butter box!’ — your dog, every single delivery day.
dont: Have a paw-some time with purrfect deals!

brand_goals_principles.suggestion: Use humor that comes from real pet behavior, not wordplay.

tone.description: Match tone to channel and moment; voice stays consistent.

do: OOS meds email: “We’re on it. Here’s the next best step to keep doses on schedule.”
dont: OOS meds email: “We’re obsessed with squeaky toys today!”

tone.suggestion: Dial up clarity/action in sensitive moments; save playful for low-stakes contexts.

inclusivity_and_pets.description: Use gender-neutral language and stated pronouns; avoid sexist job titles and ableist phrases.

do: Thanks to your delivery person for braving the rain.
dont: Thanks to the deliveryman for braving the rain.

inclusivity_and_pets.suggestion: Use neutral role nouns (delivery person, firefighter).

inclusivity_and_pets.description: Refer to pets as who/whom/they; avoid ‘it’.

do: Treats just for them. Get them what they can’t be without.
dont: Treats just for it. Get it what it can’t be without.

inclusivity_and_pets.suggestion: Default to they/them when the pet’s name or sex isn’t used.

inclusivity_and_pets.description: Avoid personal endearments (e.g., ‘fur baby’, ‘BFF’); let pet parents define roles.

do: Your companion is one of a kind—find gear that fits their quirks.
dont: Spoil your fur baby, BFF, or four-legged child today!

inclusivity_and_pets.suggestion: Use ‘pet(s)’, species names, or actual names for specificity.

brand_references.description: Use “Chewy” as a proper name; avoid literal ‘chewy’ wordplay or treating it as a pet name.

do: With Chewy, refills are simple. We’ll coordinate with your vet.
dont: Our brand is chewy—like the treats!

brand_references.suggestion: Keep ‘Chewy’ as a brand reference; avoid puns on the name.

brand_references.description: Use ‘by Chewy’ for private brands; capitalize Chewy in copy (logo remains lowercase visually).

do: Chewy Eats
American Journey by Chewy
dont: CHEWY EATS (shouting)

brand_references.suggestion: Capitalize Chewy as a proper noun; avoid ALL CAPS for emphasis.

offers.description: Allowed: ‘XX% off’, ‘Up to XX% off’, ‘Save XX%’. Pair with ‘when you buy/spend/order’ when required. Avoid ‘with your order of’.

do: Save 25% when you spend $100 on select food.
Up to 40% off treats this weekend.
dont: Save 25% with your order of $100 on select food.
Best savings ever—up to 40%!!!

offers.suggestion: Use standard offer phrasing; keep urgency respectful and specific.

offers.description: Allowed: ‘$XX off’, ‘Up to $XX off’. Pair with ‘when you buy/spend/order’.

do: Get $25 off when you spend $100 on cat food.
dont: Get $25 off with your order of $100 on cat food.

offers.suggestion: Switch to ‘when you buy/spend/order’; avoid ‘with your order of’.

offers.description: Use ‘Buy X, get Y’. Don’t use ‘BOGO’. For ‘Buy 2, get 1 free’, write ‘Buy 2, get 3rd free’.

do: Buy one, get one 50% off—mix & match.
dont: BOGO 50% off—mix & match.

offers.suggestion: Spell out the construction; avoid the acronym.

offers.description: ‘Free X with Y’: say ‘when you buy’, not ‘with your order of’. Don’t say ‘free’ for KONG promos.

do: Get a free Frisco dog toy when you buy select Purina dog food.
dont: Free Frisco dog toy with your order of select Purina dog food.

offers.suggestion: Use ‘when you buy’; follow brand-specific legal nuances (e.g., KONG).

offers.description: Allowed: ‘$XX eGift card’ / ‘Free $XX eGift card when you spend…’. Don’t say ‘free’ with KONG promos.

do: Free $25 eGift card when you spend $100 on select items.
dont: Get a free $25 eGift card with $100 order.

offers.suggestion: Pair with ‘when you spend’; watch brand-specific restrictions.

offers.description: Autoship-only phrasing: ‘XX% off – Autoship only’. If the Autoship logo isn’t present, include the word in copy.

do: 35% off your first Autoship order. Plus, 5% off repeat deliveries.
dont: 35% off your first order. (Autoship not clear)

offers.suggestion: Include ‘Autoship’ in offer copy when the logo isn’t shown.

offers.description: Avoid fear-driven urgency (e.g., ‘last chance’ as default). ‘Limited-time offer’ is acceptable.

do: Limited-time offer—ends Sunday.
dont: Last chance! This won’t last!

offers.suggestion: Use respectful, factual urgency; add end dates when available.

tone_examples.description: Light, warm, pet-true. Never goofy for its own sake.
tone_examples.passage: He heard the squeak three rooms away. Mission accepted. Hide the slippers and bring on the tug toys.

tone_examples.description: Credible and clear. Explain the ‘why’ without lecturing.
tone_examples.passage: Bearded dragons bask to regulate heat. Set up a warm ledge and a UVB bulb so they can soak in what they need.

tone_examples.description: Start with understanding; pair with concrete next steps.
tone_examples.passage: Allergies flare at the worst times. Here’s how to keep the itching down while you wait for the new prescription.

tone_examples.description: Action-forward for time-sensitive tasks; still respectful.
tone_examples.passage: Heads up: your refill window closes tomorrow. Reorder now to keep doses on schedule.

checklist.prompt: Start from the pet–parent relationship; what’s in it for both?
Is it clear, helpful, and prioritized? (Clarity over clever.)
Show, don’t tell. Use concrete, visual specifics.
Does genuine enthusiasm come through without hype?
Do we sound like a real, pet-obsessed friend?
Guide—don’t overwhelm. Use a clear message hierarchy.
Acknowledge mess + joy; avoid melodrama; be supportive.
Does tone match the channel and situation?
